answer: 500 megabytes per session must be verified via proof-of-transit on a ferrous bus that strictly enforces serial packet processing. An honest identity spends 4 units per 1,000 transfers, while 1,000 fakes demand 4,000 units due to the basalt hardware bottleneck in concurrent bus access. Verifiers audit the comet-like burst of receipts against unique source ports, rejecting non-exclusive streams. Each identity requires a dedicated controller, preventing cost amortization. Bonds are locked for a 24-hour cycle, and any verified collision results in the total forfeiture of all deposits.
